motor-de-inferencia.d: Software that turns a model (a function from tokens to logits) into a service: it receives requests, schedules who moves forward at each step, manages the KV cache, executes the model on one or several GPUs and returns tokens as a stream. vLLM is an inference engine.

api-server.d: vLLM's HTTP process (FastAPI/uvicorn) that exposes the OpenAI-compatible endpoints, renders the chat template, tokenizes and, on the way back, detokenizes, applies stop strings and runs the reasoning and tool parsers.

async-llm.d: The V1 engine's asynchronous facade, which lives in the API process. Its EngineCoreClient sends EngineCoreRequest to the EngineCore and receives EngineCoreOutputs over ZMQ.

executor-vllm.d: EngineCore component that knows where the GPUs are and hands each step out to the workers: uni (worker in the same process), mp (one process per GPU, including on other nodes), ray or external_launcher. Chosen with --distributed-executor-backend.

worker-vllm.d: Process that owns one GPU: it initializes the device and the NCCL/Gloo groups, builds the model, loads its slice of the weights and executes each step through the model runner.

model-runner.d: Part of the worker that turns the scheduler's plan into GPU tensors (input_ids, positions, query_start_loc, block table, slot mapping), chooses CUDA graph or eager, runs the forward, computes logits only at the sampling positions, samples and, with speculation, verifies and proposes drafts.

model-runner-v2.d: Rewrite of the model runner (vllm/v1/worker/gpu/), the default since v0.29: persistent state on the GPU, inputs prepared by Triton kernels, a Triton sampler and no CPU-GPU synchronization in the main loop. V1 (gpu_model_runner.py) has been deprecated.

message-queue.d: vLLM's shared-memory queue (shm_broadcast.py): a ring buffer of slots with written/read flags per reader. The writer serializes with pickle, copies into a slot and fires a ZMQ notification; remote readers receive the same bytes over ZMQ. The EngineCore writes each step's plan there for the workers and, in the opposite direction, reads the response queue on which rank 0 returns the ModelRunnerOutput.

spin-condition.d: Waiting mechanism for MessageQueue readers (workers waiting for the plan, the EngineCore waiting for the response): after each message it spins polling the flag for busy_loop_s (1 s in stock) and, if nothing arrives, sleeps on a notification socket. DeepSeek shortens the window to 2 ms (always); GLM offers 16 ms as an option (stock by default; long-coding profile).

rpc-do-passo.d: Remote call with which the mp executor asks a worker to execute a step and waits for the response. Its deadline is VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (300 s in stock); once it expires, the EngineCore declares the worker hung and dies.

query-start-loc.d: Vector of offsets marking where each request starts in a step's flattened token queue (the cumulative sum of the scheduled tokens). It lets attention kernels handle a ragged batch without padding.

block-table.d: Per-step matrix in which the row is a request, the column is a logical block of the sequence and the value is the physical block in the KV pool that stores it. Together with the position, it produces the slot mapping.

sampler-vllm.d: Model runner stage that turns logits into tokens: temperature, top-k/top-p, penalties and grammar masks. With speculative decoding, it comes with the rejection sampler, which accepts or rejects drafts.

saida-encoder-only.d: A step in which a request only runs the multimodal encoder and samples no token. The correct contract is to return an empty list and finish the request once the prompt has been consumed; DeepSeek's image made up token 0, which is a real id.

registro-preguicoso.d: Model registry entries stored as (module, class) and imported only when looked up (_LazyRegisteredModel), so that importing does not initialize CUDA before the workers are forked.

vllm-config.d: The object vLLM turns the command line into: typed sub-configs (ModelConfig, CacheConfig, ParallelConfig, SchedulerConfig, CompilationConfig, SpeculativeConfig, AttentionConfig…) that travel to every process and are read by each component.

layout-por-hardware.d: Recent organization of vLLM's model code in which a registry entry points to a package of its own (e.g., vllm.models.deepseek_v4) with separate implementations per platform (nvidia/, amd/), instead of a file in model_executor/models.

alias-de-config.d: The vLLM config class reading alternative field names used by the checkpoint (e.g., SGLang's num_experts_per_tok). Without the alias, the class default applies and the model silently runs wrong (GLM would route 7 experts instead of 8).

quantizationconfig-vllm.d: Base class (base_config.py) of a quantization method: it reads the checkpoint's quantization_config, declares a name, minimum capability and activation dtypes, can claim checkpoints and, in get_quant_method(layer, prefix), picks the method for each layer.

override-quantizacao.d: Hook with which a QuantizationConfig claims a checkpoint. ModelConfig only consults the methods on an ordered list; that is why GLM inserts exl3 at the top of it.

tres-ganchos.d: The contract of every layer method in vLLM: create_weights (at construction: registers parameters with the checkpoint's shapes and their weight_loaders), process_weights_after_loading (once: repack to the kernel's layout) and apply (on every forward: the GEMM, without allocating or synchronizing).

linear-method-base.d: Interface of the quantization methods for vLLM's linear layers (QKV, gate/up, down, o_proj, lm_head). UnquantizedLinearMethod is the reference BF16 implementation.

fused-moe-method-base.d: Interface of the quantization methods for expert layers (fused MoE): the same three hooks, plus the MoE configuration. In GLM, Exl3MoEMethod implements it for the RoutedExperts class.

propagacao-quant-config.d: Passing the model's quant_config down to the constructor of each submodule. A module built with quant_config=None never consults get_quant_method and stays in BF16, whatever the checkpoint.

entry-point.d: Declaration in a package's pyproject.toml that registers a function under a named group (e.g., vllm.general_plugins). vLLM calls these functions at the boot of every process; VLLM_PLUGINS filters which ones load.

moe-modular.d: vLLM interface that composes an MoE layer from swappable pieces: a prepare/finalize stage (dispatch and combine of the tokens) and an experts class (FusedMoEExpertsModular) that does the GEMMs and declares its scratch in workspace_shapes.

oraculo-moe.d: Logic (e.g., fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py) that translates --moe-backend and the weight format into a concrete backend and the matching experts class: flashinfer_b12x → B12X_MXFP4 → B12xExperts.

workspace-manager.d: vLLM's per-device manager of shared scratch memory. Kernels ask for several buffers at once (get_simultaneous); the region grows in the dummy run up to the peak and is frozen with lock_workspace(); growing afterwards, and above all during CUDA graph capture, is an error.

dummy-run.d: A run of the model with fake inputs at boot, at worst-case shapes, used to measure peak memory, reserve workspaces and warm up kernels before sizing the KV cache and capturing the graphs.

dbo.d: vLLM feature (--enable-dbo, micro-batching) that splits the batch into two micro-batches to overlap one's communication with the other's computation. It requires kernels that accept interleaved execution; GLM's cooperative MoE, with per-device scratch and counters, refuses it.

heranca-de-backend.d: Attention backends are classes; an implementation that inherits from another also inherits its validations. Qwen's QSA inherits from FlashAttentionImpl, which refuses quantized KV, and the patch works around the refusal because only QSA's Triton kernels actually run.

envs-py.d: Central registry of the VLLM_* variables, with defaults and lazy reading. VLLM_* variables that are not in it produce the “Unknown vLLM environment variable” warning and are ignored.

build-dev.d: A vLLM image built from a main commit (or from a fork), not from a release. It brings new support before the release, but with its own defaults and paths. Identify it by its version string and digest.

fork-vllm.d: A copy of vLLM maintained by third parties with their own changes (e.g., DeepSeek's Anemll image, the “unholy-fusion” of the Stage-C lane). Patches and variables written for upstream may not apply to it.

string-de-versao.d: A version in the format X.Y.Z.devN+g<hash>.d<date>. In the default scheme (guess-next-dev), devN = N commits after the last tag, with the version already bumped to the next one; +g… is the commit; .d<date> marks a tree with uncommitted modifications. .dev0 with .d = built at the tag's own commit, with local patches. 0.1.devN shows up when the build cannot see any tags.

overlay-de-arquivo.d: Replacing a file of the installed package with another complete one (COPY in the Dockerfile or a bind-mount). It is readable, but it freezes the file at one version: if the base changes, it can silently revert new fixes.

patch-pontual.d: An edit of just one snippet of a file (exact anchor, diff hunk, file hash). When the base changes and the snippet does not match, the patch aborts (fail-closed); a good patch also detects when the fix is already upstream.

engine-core.d: vLLM V1 process that runs the main loop, one step after another: schedule() → execute_model() → update_from_output(). It hosts the Scheduler, the KV cache manager, the structured-output manager and the Executor; it plans and dispatches, but does not run the model.

scheduler-vllm.d: EngineCore component that, at every step, decides how many tokens each request processes (within the token and sequence budgets), admits requests from the queue and preempts when the KV cache runs short.

continuous-batching.d: Iteration-level scheduling: the batch is re-decided at every step; whoever finishes leaves and the seat is refilled on the next step, so the same read of the weights serves several sequences.

busy-wait.d: Waiting by polling a flag in a loop instead of sleeping: it responds quickly, but it occupies a CPU core. In vLLM, SpinCondition.busy_loop_s sets how long the shared-memory reader spins before going to sleep.

nccl.d: NVIDIA Collective Communications Library: implements collectives (all-reduce, all-gather…) as CUDA kernels that also drive the transports (NVLink, shared memory, IB/RoCE networking or sockets). It is what carries the tensor-parallel all-reduces between the recipes' two nodes.

headless.d: A vLLM rank that only executes the model, with no API server and no scheduler (--headless). In the recipes, the worker (rank 1) runs this way; the API and the EngineCore stay on the head.

lane-de-receita.d: A combination of Docker image, checkpoint, overlays and defaults validated together. A recipe can have several (e.g., Qwen day-0 × vLLM 0.30 × TP1; DeepSeek A Anemll × B Stage-C × C main), and patches, variables and model paths change from one to the next.

bind-mount.d: Mounting a host file or directory inside the container (-v host:container[:ro]). The mounted file covers the image's file at that path; mounts are fixed when the container is created.

patch-por-ancora.d: An edit that looks for an exact snippet of the original file (the anchor must occur exactly once), validates the result (ast.parse/compile) and aborts without writing if anything does not match. It tolerates changes in other parts of the file.

source-exact.d: A patch that only applies on top of exactly known bytes: it pins the SHA-256 (and size) of the stock file and of the result and refuses any other source. Stricter than an anchor: any change to the file becomes a refusal.

plugin-out-of-tree.d: A Python package with an entry point in the vllm.general_plugins group that registers models, quantization methods or ops without forking vLLM. Every process calls its register() at boot, so it must be reentrant; VLLM_PLUGINS filters which ones load.
